GK-04.c01: A **defect** is something broken, worn, missing or not working right.
**Out-of-service (OOS)** is an official order that the vehicle may not be driven until repaired.
The **motor carrier** is the company that runs the vehicle, usually your employer.
GK-04.c02: **Safety** is the most important reason to inspect, for you and everyone else on the road.
Finding defects early also prevents breakdowns, lost time and money, and crashes.
Drivers must inspect under both **federal and state law**.
Federal and state inspectors may inspect too; an unsafe vehicle is placed **out-of-service** until repaired.
GK-04.c03: Pre-trip → inspect every time and read the **last vehicle inspection report**; the carrier must fix and **certify** each safety item.
Once you drive, safe operation is **your** job, **not the mechanic's**, because you are the one in control.
During the trip → watch gauges and **look, listen, smell and feel**; check tires, brakes, lights, connections, coupling and cargo securement at every stop.
After the trip → at the end of the trip, day or tour of duty, inspect **each vehicle you drove**.
GK-04.c04: Front tires need at least **4/32 inch** tread in every major groove; all other tires at least **2/32 inch**.
**Rust around wheel nuts** can mean they are loose; a wheel or rim **repaired by welding** is unsafe.
Steering play of **more than 10 degrees** (about **2 inches** on a 20-inch wheel) makes the vehicle hard to steer.
Missing **¼ or more** of a spring's leaves = **out-of-service**; a broken exhaust can let poisonous fumes into the cab.
**Three** kinds of emergency equipment are required: fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless circuit breakers), and warning devices like **3 red reflective triangles**.
GK-04.c05: To get a CDL you must pass a hands-on **vehicle inspection test** at a real vehicle.
For each item, **point to or touch it, name it, and explain why** you check it.
Trucks → before every trip, check the truck is **not overloaded** and the load is **balanced and secured**; with HazMat, check papers and placards.
GK-04.c06: Always follow the **same order** (approach, then 7 steps); in Step 2, first make sure **parking brakes are on** and/or wheels are chocked.
Air pressure should build from **50 to 90 psi within 3 minutes**, up to governor cut-out, usually **120–140 psi**.
Oil pressure must be normal **within seconds**; temperatures rise gradually; the **ABS** light should go out, and staying on means a fault.
Step 4 → engine off, take the **key** with you; front clearance lights and reflectors are **amber**, rear ones red.
Hydraulic leak test → pump **3 times**, **hold 5 seconds**; service brake test at about 5 mph; check brake, turn and 4-way lights separately.
GK-04.c07: During a trip, check instruments, gauges, mirrors, tires, lights and cargo, and investigate anything you **see, hear, smell or feel**.
Check cargo securement within the **first 50 miles**, then every **150 miles or 3 hours, whichever comes first**.
Cargo shifts and tie-downs loosen as you drive, which is why the checks repeat.
GK-04.c08: You may have to write a **daily report** on each vehicle you drove, listing anything affecting **safety** or that could cause a breakdown.
The carrier uses the report to plan repairs.
Keep a copy **in the vehicle for 1 day**, so the next driver can learn about the problems.
